data.why: The interface takes pasted Sanskrit text directly (Devanagari or IAST); no file upload is involved, and the README's own example (वाग्देव्यै नमः) is shown as placeholder text in the input box.

goals: Paste a Sanskrit sentence and get automatic word segmentation (padaccheda) that resolves sandhi and compound splits
Read morphological tags (case, gender, number, tense, mood, voice) for each segmented word
Click through a word or lemma to a dictionary (Ambuda, Kosha.app, Sanskrit Kosha) or to the Ashtadhyayi dhatu index for verbs
Compare the Dharmamitra model against the Hellwig/Skrutable model on the same sentence, especially one full of compounds
Transliterate the input and its analysis into a different output script (e.g. Devanagari, Grantha, Bengali, SLP1)
Inspect the syllable (akshara) and character (varna) breakdown of the input text

review.summary: The tree captures what Sakhaa is for: segmentation with sandhi and compound splitting, tagging in the Paninian style, comparing the two engines, dictionary and dhatu links, transliteration, and the akshara breakdown. Most screens back their nodes. It needs a few fixes before filing: t7's evidence tests the wrong link, multi-sentence passage input was never tried, there is one padding phase, and check.json's screen references don't match this run.
